# Copilot Instructions

<!-- Generated by gspec explore — edit freely, this is your file -->

## Coding Conventions

- Keep the game framework-free. Add behavior inside the existing HTML plus single-module JavaScript structure unless a concrete requirement justifies splitting files.
- Put tunable gameplay behavior in top-level exported constants when possible instead of scattering magic numbers through the update loop or rendering code.
- Keep reusable game math and rule decisions as exported pure functions so they can be tested directly.
- Model stateful gameplay entities with factory functions that return plain objects containing state plus `update()` and `draw()` methods. Match the `createLM()` and `createCSM()` pattern.
- Let `createGameController()` own DOM reads and writes, localStorage access, overlay flow, and the frame loop. Keep browser-specific side effects out of pure helpers.
- Preserve the existing `localGameState` gating pattern for runtime flow.
- Reuse the existing feedback channels first: HUD text, overlays, color changes, particles, and sound callbacks.
- Keep persistence lightweight and local. Extend the localStorage-backed profile structures rather than introducing a heavier storage layer.
- Preserve the current retro NASA arcade aesthetic unless the feature explicitly changes the presentation.
- Gracefully degrade optional browser APIs such as audio instead of crashing when unavailable.

## Testing Conventions

- Put pure logic tests under `tests/unit/` and browser or controller behavior under `tests/component/`.
- Import named exports from `game.js` directly when testing helpers or factories.
- Write small focused assertions around one behavior at a time, matching the current short `it(...)` style.
- Use the existing JSDOM setup helpers for mocked canvas and audio behavior.
- Preserve or improve the current coverage thresholds from `vitest.config.js`.
